description: Samsung SSD and memory card toolkit: firmware updates, drive health, benchmark, secure erase and performance settings.
notes: Not portable and not silent: Samsung's installer refuses silent mode on purpose and asks
whether you live in a GDPR country or Brazil. Scoop opens the setup wizard; finish it yourself.
Install, update and uninstall from an elevated (admin) shell.
The installer adds the SamsungMagicianSVC service, the magdrv kernel driver, a scheduled task
'SamsungMagician' that starts Magician at logon, and may switch the Windows power plan.
Magician can update itself; prefer 'scoop update Samsung-Magician' so Scoop knows the installed version.
Only 'scoop uninstall Samsung-Magician' removes Magician from the system.
A fresh install stops if Samsung Magician is already installed without Scoop. To let Scoop take over that copy,
run $env:GESU_ALLOW_EXISTING = '1' in the same shell and install again.
pre_install: if (!(is_admin)) { error "$app installs a driver and a service: run this from an elevated shell."; break }
# A fresh 'scoop install' must not silently take over a copy installed without Scoop; 'scoop update' is not affected.

error "$($existing.DisplayName) ($($existing.DisplayVersion)) is already installed on this system. Uninstall it first, or run `$env:GESU_ALLOW_EXISTING = '1' and install again to let Scoop install over it and manage it from now on."

script: Write-Host 'Samsung Magician does not allow silent installation: finish the setup wizard that opens now.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
if ($setup.ExitCode -ne 0) { error "Samsung Magician setup exited with code $($setup.ExitCode) (2 or 5: cancelled)."; break }
if (!(is_admin)) { error "$app runs a driver and a service: run this from an elevated shell."; break }
# On update the new installer upgrades in place; only a real uninstall removes the app.
if (!$entry) { warn 'Samsung Magician was not found among installed programs; nothing to remove.'; return }
